the cause, measured, and how I fix it

Both things you said were right. The calendar was painted behind the notes box (I dropped its stacking order when merging two positioners last round), and the last column was clipped: the grid asked for 7 columns of 32px plus 6 gaps = 248px inside a grid only 216px wide, so Saturday sat past the edge and the panel clips overflow. Measured: 5 days past the edge, and the last one was not clickable.

Fix: the columns share whatever width the panel has. Measured after: 0 past the edge, all clickable, at 360 / 390 / 430 / 768 / 1440 / 1920.

the cause, measured, and how I fix it

Reproduced on your exact path — open a task, press +, press Save. No other step. On your build the alarm is gone; after a full reload the task has 0 reminders and reopening shows nothing.

Cause, and it is mine: the Edit window keeps its own copy of the alarm list, taken when the window opens, and Save writes that copy over the task. My fix last round added the alarm somewhere else, so Save overwrote it with the stale, empty copy.

Fix: one owner — the window's list is the only list, and everything that adds an alarm adds to it. Measured on the fix: 1 reminder after Save and a full page reload, and it is there when you reopen the task.

A pasted snapshot does not save in either notes section

live

LIVE — in your planner now, build 2026-09-23 12:41

Where: the Journal → Notes tab → + New note, and the notes box inside a task's Edit window.

"regarding adding a picture in notes, it still doesn't work."

2026-09-22, round 2 "Number four, you're looking at the wrong thing. I'm referring to the notes section in journal."

2026-09-23 "I want it in both, in the journal notes and in the edit notes."

2026-09-23, later "Inside the notes section in the edit, and inside the notes section in the journal under notes. Whenever I open a new note, if I add a picture in there where I copy paste it from a snapshot, it does not save. That needs to be featured correctly."

2026-09-23, round 3 "All I care about is that it works. You should just show an imaginary picture on the after. Make sure the paste of any picture would actually work there."

2026-09-23, round 4 Approved.

what I want to check with you

Pictures are stored inside your planner so they survive a reload and work offline, which grows your saved file — a phone snapshot is roughly 100-300 KB each. Should I shrink anything wider than about 1200px before storing it? I would, unless you need them full size.

the cause, measured, and how I fix it

Found the exact screen you mean, and the two halves fail differently.

The Journal note cannot hold a picture at all. Journal → Notes → + New note opens a plain <textarea> (569×150, the box that says "Write anything"). A textarea is text-only by nature — measured: pasting a snapshot into it gives 0 pictures and 0 characters. Nothing happens, and no paste handler could ever change that.

The task notes box takes the picture but the task looks empty. The paste works there (1 picture, and it survives a reload) — but the "this task has notes" pen mark is decided by stripping every tag and asking whether any TEXT is left. A note that is only a picture reads as empty, so no mark appears and the task looks exactly as if you pasted nothing.

Built and measured, all three halves:
• the Journal note box is now the same kind of rich box the task notes use — a snapshot pastes straight in
• copying from a browser works too, and the picture is FETCHED AND STORED inside the note rather than left as a link, so it survives going offline or the page disappearing
• a picture now counts as a note, so the task shows its pen mark

Proven: snapshot paste → 1 picture; browser paste → 2 pictures; and after a full page reload the note still shows both. Your existing notes are untouched — the text is still stored as text, the pictures sit alongside it.

The picture shows: the exact screen you described — Journal → Notes → + New note — with a snapshot pasted into "Write anything". Same paste in both pictures: nothing on your build, the picture on the fix

measured, both ways

your build → paste a snapshot → 0 pictures, 0 characters
the fix → paste a snapshot → 1 picture
the fix → paste from a browser → 2 pictures
the fix → FULL RELOAD → both pictures still there

The picture in the AFTER is a stand-in screenshot, as you asked — what matters is that a real paste lands in the box and is still there when you come back.
